doc.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview

title: Finding his own bass sound and teaching Malachi Favors
summary: Ware took a bit from Blanton and Israel Crosby, and shows young Malachi Favors what he knew.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Now there was a whole lot of musicians who hate to copy, you know, the creative musicians. I mean, that wasn't it. Just like, me, speaking about myself, now I loved Blanton, I loved him, and I took a little bit from Blanton, took a little bit from Israel Crosby and I put a little bit of Wilbur Ware in there, so I believe I got my own little way of playing, you know? So that's me. I don't find, like I hear people come up, saying, "You don't sound like so and so and so and so .." and I say, "Yeah, I have to sound like me."

I had a good friend of mine, a young bassist -- a Malachi Favors, with the Chicago Art Ensemble, and Maul brilliant young bassist, younger than I am Wilbur and he used to come for me every morning, and say, "Let's just play something for me." He stayed maybe 2 or 3 blocks from where I was living in Chicago during that time, '48, and I played and he was learning. You know, I'd show him what I knew, and now like I say, technically, I didn't know too much, but playing around -- Israel was showing how to hold my hand correct, you know, and I was watching people that was holding their hands correct.
